items.title: Nvidia stock rebounds after board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
points: Nvidia's stock rebounded after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO effective immediately, reversing investor uncertainty around leadership.
The news sparked gains across tech stocks and prompted rotation into technology shares amid lingering AI bubble concerns.

items.title: Major U.S. indices surge for the week
points: Dow Jones +5.47%, S&P 500 +5.61%, Nasdaq Composite +6.68% for the week.
CBOE Volatility Index (VIX, a measure of expected stock market swings) plummeted 33.7% to 23.81, indicating reduced market anxiety despite ongoing concerns.

items.title: Core PCE inflation comes in hotter than expected
points: Core PCE price index (the Personal Consumption Expenditures index excluding food and energy, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge) rose to 3.3% year-over-year in October, above the 3.2% consensus forecast.
The hotter reading resurfaced debate about an AI bubble, with investors worried that massive AI infrastructure spending may not deliver timely returns, drawing parallels to the dot-com crash era.
Market volatility reflected conflicting signals as traders balanced growth optimism against inflation and valuation concerns.

items.title: Analyst downgrades hit AI-related semiconductor names
points: Analysts issued downgrades on AMD, Broadcom, and Sandisk amid profitability concerns tied to AI spending.
AMD dropped 13%, Broadcom fell 10%, and Sandisk fell 10% as the AI bubble debate resurfaced.
Energy stocks underperformed at +1.5% despite Oil WTI holding steady near $83.33/barrel, as investors rotated into tech instead.

items.title: Sector and stock performance highlights
points: Information Technology led sector gains at +7.3%, Materials climbed +7.9%, while Consumer Staples lagged at +2.4%.
Top individual gainers included CoStar Group (+22%), Axon Enterprise (+18%), and Global Payments (+16%).

headlines: Nvidia stock rebounds after board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, sparking fresh gains across tech stocks amid lingering AI bubble concerns.

Analyst calls highlight AI-related caution with downgrades on semiconductor names AMD, Broadcom, and Sandisk amid profitability concerns.

sections.title: Market Rally and Nvidia's Leadership Shift
points: 1. Nvidia's stock rebounded significantly after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO effective immediately, reversing investor uncertainty around leadership.
2. The broader market responded positively: Dow Jones added 5.47%, S&P 500 climbed 5.61%, and Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.68% for the week.
3. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX, a measure of expected stock market swings) fell 33.7% to 23.81, indicating reduced market anxiety despite ongoing concerns.

sections.title: Inflation Data and AI Bubble Debate
points: 1. Core PCE price index (the Personal Consumption Expenditures index excluding food and energy, used by the Federal Reserve for inflation decisions) rose to 3.3% year-over-year in October, exceeding the 3.2% forecast.

2. The hotter-than-expected inflation reading resurfaced debate about an AI bubble as investors worry massive capital investments in AI infrastructure may not deliver timely returns, drawing parallels to the dot-com crash era.
3. Market volatility reflected conflicting signals: stocks swung both higher and lower during the week as traders balanced growth optimism against inflation and valuation concerns.

sections.title: Sector Performance and Notable Stock Moves
points: 1. Information Technology led sector gains at +7.3%, while Materials stocks climbed 7.9%; Consumer Staples lagged at +2.4%.
2. Top gainers included CoStar Group (+22%), Axon Enterprise (+18%), and Global Payments (+16%), while semiconductor names faced headwinds: AMD -13%, Broadcom -10%, and Sandisk -10%.
3. Energy stocks underperformed at +1.5% despite Oil WTI holding steady near $83.33/barrel, as investors rotated toward technology on the Huang reinstatement news.
